mainTopic: Widths of roads, burial rights, the mourners' standing-and-sitting ceremony, and the standard size of a burial cave
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about road widths. A public road is 16 אמות wide, and a road to ערי מקלט is 32 אמות. רב הונא learns the doubling from the word 'הַדֶּרֶךְ' in the פסוק. The גמרא then explains why the king's road and the road to a grave have no fixed width. A ברייתא teaches that a man's family may bury him in the grave plot he sold, to avoid פגם משפחה. Next comes the custom of seven מעמדות ומושבות for the dead, and רבי יהודה's description of how it was done in Judea. A story about רב אויא leads רב יוסף, אביי and רבא to set limits on when, where and for whom the ceremony is done. The גמרא then defends those limits against a challenge from שבת. Finally, a new משנה begins giving the standard size of a burial cave and its eight niches.

steps.title: Widths of the public road and the road to the cities of refuge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list: a public road is 16 אמות wide, and a road to ערי מקלט is 32 אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: A public road is sixteen cubits wide. A road to the cities of refuge is thirty-two cubits wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing a list from a ברייתא of how wide different roads must be. These are the last two items: the public road and the road leading to ערי מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each road in the list gets a fixed minimum width. The road to ערי מקלט is exactly double the public road. The next steps explain where that doubling comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A public road used by many people
Cities of refuge, where a person who killed by accident could run to be safe
Cubits, a measure of length (roughly half a meter each)

phrases.english: A public road is sixteen cubits wide.

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ עָרֵי מִקְלָט – שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: A road to the cities of refuge is thirty-two cubits wide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא listing road widths that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public road is 16 אמות wide; a road to ערי מקלט is 32 אמות wide.

steps.title: רב הונא asks for the source of the 32 cubits
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks which פסוק teaches that the road to ערי מקלט must be 32 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is the verse that teaches this?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks for the source in the תורה for the 32-אמה rule. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The width of 32 is not obvious, so רב הונא looks for a פסוק behind it. He is not challenging the rule, only asking where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (a request for the source in the תורה)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: What is the verse for this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the 32-אמה width from step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that the road to ערי מקלט is 32 אמות wide?

steps.title: The extra word in the verse doubles the road
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'הדרך' (the way) instead of just 'דרך' (a way). The extra letter teaches a double road: 16 + 16 = 32.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You shall prepare for yourself the way.' It says 'the way' and not just 'a way.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his own question with the פסוק about preparing the road to ערי מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'דרך'. Saying 'הדרך' adds something, which is read as a second road on top of the first. Two public roads of 16 make 32.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall prepare for yourself the way' (the פסוק about the road to ערי מקלט)

steps.whatToRemember: Road to ערי מקלט = 32 אמות, double a public road, learned from 'הַדֶּרֶךְ' instead of 'דֶּרֶךְ'.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'You shall prepare for yourself the way'
Not just 'a way' but 'the way.'
phrases.notes: The extra ה is read as adding a second road, so the width doubles from 16 to 32.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's question from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'תכין לך הדרך' uses 'הדרך' rather than 'דרך', which teaches a double road: 32 אמות.

steps.title: Why the king's road has no limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the king's road has no fixed width. It explains that a king may break through a fence to make a road, and no one may stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A king's road has no set measure. This is because a king may break through a fence to make a road for himself, and no one may protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and explains it. The king's road has no limit because the king may take land for a road whenever he needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary roads have a fixed width because private owners' rights must be respected. A king has the power to break through private fences, so his road can be as wide as he needs.

keyTerms.meaning: No one may protest or stop him

phrases.english: A king's road has no set measure.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ פּוֹרֵץ גָּדֵר לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ דֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: Because a king may break through a fence to make a road for himself,
and no one may protest against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא back to the משנה's list of roads.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king's road has no fixed width, because the king may break through fences to make a road and no one may protest.

steps.title: Why the road to a grave has no limit
steps.stepSummary: The road for a funeral procession to a grave has no fixed width, because of the honor of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: A road to a grave has no set measure, because of the honor of the deceased.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and gives a short reason for it: respect for the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A funeral may draw a large crowd, and limiting the road would shame the deceased. So the road's width follows the needs of the funeral, not a fixed number.

keyTerms.meaning: The road to a grave, used by the funeral procession

phrases.english: A road to a grave has no set measure.
Because of the honor of the deceased.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next line of the משנה, explained the same way as step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The road to a grave has no fixed width, out of honor for the deceased.

steps.title: The משנה about the standing place for comforting mourners
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the judges of ציפורי said the מעמד must be an area of בית ארבע קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The standing place: the judges of ציפורי said it is an area for sowing four קבין of seed, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about the מעמד. This sets up a ברייתא on a related topic about burial places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a size for the area where people stand after a burial to comfort the mourners. The גמרא does not discuss the size here. Instead it uses this line to bring a ברייתא about selling burial-related places.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where people stand after a burial to comfort the mourners
The judges of the city of ציפורי
An area big enough to sow four קבין of seed

phrases.english: The standing place: the judges of Tzippori said:
An area for sowing four kav, and so on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the משנה, opening the topic of burial areas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The judges of ציפורי set the מעמד at an area of בית ארבע קבין.

steps.title: A family may bury their relative in the grave he sold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a man sold his grave, the road to it, his מעמד, or his eulogy place, his family may still bury him there against the buyer's will. This is to avoid פגם משפחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone sold his grave, the road to his grave, his standing place, or his eulogy place, his family members may come and bury him there against the buyer's will, because of the shame to the family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about burial places. It rules that a sale of a man's own grave plot does not stop his family from burying him there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a sale passes full rights to the buyer. Here the family's honor wins: if a member were buried apart from the family, it would shame the family. So they may use the grave and its connected places even though he sold them.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the eulogy is given
Shame or damage to the family's name

steps.confusionAlert: 'עַל כׇּרְחוֹ' means against the will of the buyer, not the person who died.
steps.whatToRemember: Family honor (פגם משפחה) lets relatives bury a man in his family grave plot even after he sold it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a family's honor can limit a buyer's ordinary rights to land he purchased.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who sells his grave, the road to his grave,
his standing place, or his eulogy place,
the family members may come
and bury him there against his will,
phrases.notes: 'His will' means the buyer's will. The family can bury him even if the buyer objects.

phrases.english: because of the shame to the family.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to the מעמד and other burial places in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a man sold his grave or its connected places, his family may still bury him there against the buyer's will, because of פגם משפחה.

steps.title: At least seven standings and sittings for the dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that we do no fewer than seven מעמדות ומושבות for the dead, matching the seven 'הבל' in the פסוק in קהלת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: We do no fewer than seven standings and sittings for the dead, matching the פסוק 'Vanity of vanities, says קהלת, vanity of vanities, all is vanity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about a mourning custom: the people coming back from the burial stop, sit, and stand at least seven times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number seven comes from the פסוק in קהלת. 'הבל' counts as one and each plural 'הבלים' counts as two, so the פסוק has seven. This connects to step 7, which mentioned a person's מעמד as part of his burial rights.

keyTerms.meaning: Standings and sittings — stops made by the mourners for the dead
We do not do fewer than

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
We do not make fewer than seven
standings and sittings for the dead,
corresponding to "Vanity of vanities, says Kohelet,
vanity of vanities, all is vanity."
phrases.notes: Count them: each 'הבל' is one and each plural 'הבלים' is two, so you get seven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of the מעמד in step 7 and teaches the custom connected to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At least seven מעמדות ומושבות are made for the dead, based on the seven 'הבל' in קהלת.

steps.title: How is the ceremony actually done?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי how the standings and sittings are actually carried out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: How do they do it?
steps.whatsHappening: A practical question about the custom we just learned. It sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave the number seven but did not say what happens at each stop. רב אחא wants to know what the people actually do.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said
to Rav Ashi: How do they do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical details of the custom taught in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is actually done during the seven standings and sittings.

steps.title: רבי יהודה describes the custom in Judea
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers with a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that in Judea someone would call out 'Stand, dear ones, stand' and 'Sit, dear ones, sit.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said: In Judea, at first they would make no fewer than seven standings and sittings for the dead, by saying things like 'Stand, dear ones, stand' and 'Sit, dear ones, sit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by quoting a ברייתא that describes what was said at each stop.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At each stop, someone tells the mourners to stand and later tells them to sit. The word 'בראשונה' (at first) shows this was the old practice in Judea.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: He said to him: As it was taught,
Rabbi Yehuda said: In Judea,
at first they would not make fewer
than seven standings and sittings for the dead,
for example: "Stand, dear ones, stand";
"Sit, dear ones, sit."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At each stop someone calls out 'Stand, dear ones, stand' and 'Sit, dear ones, sit.'

steps.title: The רבנן: then it would be allowed even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן respond to רבי יהודה: if that is all the custom involves, it should be allowed even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If so, it should be permitted to do this even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, the רבנן push back on רבי יהודה's description and point out what it would lead to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ceremony is only telling people to stand and sit, there is no eulogy or mourning in it. Then nothing should stop it from being done on שבת. The challenge suggests the real custom must involve something more.

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
even on Shabbat it would be permitted to do so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the description of the custom given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's description of the ceremony as just calling out 'stand' and 'sit'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ceremony has no real mourning in it, it would be allowed on שבת, so the description seems incomplete.

steps.title: רב אויא does the ceremony for his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tells a story: רב אויא's wife, the sister of רמי בר פפא, died, and he made a מעמד ומושב for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sister of רמי בר פפא was married to רב אויא. She died, and he made a standing and sitting ceremony for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It sets up the critiques of רב יוסף, אביי and רבא that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story gives a real case of the ceremony. The next steps use it to teach when, where and for whom the ceremony should be done.

phrases.english: The sister of Rami bar Pappa
was married to Rav Avya.
She died, and he made a standing and sitting for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרָמֵי בַּר פָּפָּא הֲוָה נְסִיבָא לֵיהּ לְרַב אַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule to a real-life case of the ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אויא performed a מעמד ומושב for his wife.

steps.title: רב יוסף: he made two mistakes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says רב אויא erred twice: the ceremony is only for close relatives, and only on the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: He erred in two things. He erred, because it is done only for close relatives, and he did it even for distant ones. And he erred, because it is done only on the first day, and he did it on the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף criticizes רב אויא and points out two rules he broke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From his criticism we learn two limits on the ceremony. It is done only by close family, and only on the first day, the day of the burial. רב אויא did it with more distant relatives and on the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day (the day of burial)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: He erred in two things;
he erred, since it is done only with close relatives,
and he did it even with distant ones;

phrases.aramaic: וּטְעָה – שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: and he erred, since it is done only on the first day,
phrases.notes: The first day means the day of the burial.

phrases.english: and he did it on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates רב אויא's action from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ceremony is done only by close relatives and only on the first day.

steps.title: אביי: he also erred about the place
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a third mistake: the ceremony is done only in the cemetery, and רב אויא did it in the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He also erred in this, because it is done only in the cemetery, and he did it in the city.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another mistake to רב יוסף's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaches a new limit about location. The ceremony belongs at the cemetery, not in town.

phrases.english: Abaye said: He also erred in this –
since it is done only in the cemetery,
and he did it in the city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third mistake to the two named by רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ceremony is done only in the cemetery.

steps.title: רבא: he also erred about local custom
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds another mistake: the ceremony is done only where it is the custom, and in רב אויא's place it was not the custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He also erred in this, because it is done only in a place where people have this custom, and there it was not the custom.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds one more mistake, about local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ceremony is not required everywhere. It depends on what is customary in that place, and where רב אויא lived people did not do it.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place where it is the custom

steps.whatToRemember: The seven standings and sittings are done only by close relatives, only on the day of burial, only at the cemetery, and only where it is the local custom. רב אויא broke all of these limits.

phrases.english: Rava said: He also erred in this –
since it is done only in a place where it is the custom,
and there it was not the custom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth mistake, completing the list of critiques of רב אויא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ceremony is done only in places where it is the custom.

steps.title: Bringing back the רבנן's words as a challenge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises an objection to רב יוסף and אביי from the ברייתא's line: 'if so, it should be allowed even on שבת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: The רבנן said to him: If so, it should be allowed to do this even on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again the רבנן's reply to רבי יהודה, now as an attack on רב יוסף and אביי. This line sets up the challenge, and the next step explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, this line was the רבנן arguing with רבי יהודה. Now the גמרא uses it for something new. The רבנן were talking about doing the ceremony on שבת, so it must be possible for it to come up on שבת. That will cause trouble for the rules of רב יוסף and אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is all it involves

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. It is the same line from step 11, quoted again to challenge רב יוסף and אביי.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: The objection is aimed at רב יוסף and אביי from the story about רב אויא.

phrases.english: They said to him: If so,
it should be permitted to do so even on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִם כֵּן, אַף בְּשַׁבָּת מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא from step 11 to challenge the limits set by רב יוסף (step 13) and אביי (step 14).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's rule (first day only) and אביי's rule (cemetery only).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן talk about the ceremony on שבת, so it must be able to happen on שבת. The next step shows why the two limits seem to rule that out.

steps.title: Why a cemetery on שבת seems impossible
steps.stepSummary: If the ceremony is only in the cemetery and only on the first day, what would anyone be doing in a cemetery on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is done only in the cemetery and only on the first day, then what would anyone be doing in a cemetery on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge. With the limits of אביי and רב יוסף, there seems to be no way the ceremony could ever happen on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not bury the dead on שבת, so nobody would be at a cemetery then. The ceremony is only on the day of burial, so the first day cannot be שבת either. That makes the רבנן's words about שבת look pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day (the day of burial)
What is he looking for? What would he be doing there?

phrases.english: And if you say it is only in the cemetery
phrases.notes: This is אביי's rule from step 14.

phrases.english: and only on the first day,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף's rule from step 13.

phrases.english: what would one be doing in a cemetery on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת וּבְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the line quoted in step 16 is a difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The combined limits of רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are no burials on שבת, so no one is in a cemetery on שבת on the day of a burial. The case the רבנן describe could then never happen.

steps.title: A burial right before שבת near the city
steps.stepSummary: The case is a city close to the cemetery, where they brought the dead person for burial at twilight before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about a city near the cemetery. They brought the dead person to be buried at twilight, right as שבת was starting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by finding a real case where the ceremony would fall on שבת, even with the limits of רב יוסף and אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burial happens on Friday at dusk, so it is still the burial day. The mourners come back from the cemetery as שבת begins, and the city is right next to it. So the ceremony could be in the cemetery area, on the first day, and also on שבת. The rules of רב יוסף and אביי stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the time between sunset and dark

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's words about שבת fit a burial at twilight on Friday near a city. So the limits of רב יוסף (first day) and אביי (in the cemetery) still hold.

phrases.english: In a city that is close to the cemetery,
where they brought him for burial at twilight.
phrases.notes: The burial is right as שבת starts, so the walk back from the cemetery happens on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 16 and 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a specific case (אוקימתא) where everything fits.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ceremony could never fall on שבת if it is only in the cemetery and only on the first day.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can fall on שבת when the burial was at twilight on Friday near a city. Both limits remain true.

steps.title: New משנה: the size of a burial cave
steps.stepSummary: If someone sells land for a burial cave, or takes a job to build one, and no size was set, the inside of the cave must be four אמות by six.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone sells land to another person so he can make a burial cave there. Or someone takes a job from another person to build him a burial cave. He must make the inside of the cave four אמות by six.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the standard size of a burial cave when the deal did not say how big it should be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two cases with the same rule: a sale of land for a cave, and a builder hired to make one. In both, when nothing was spelled out, the normal size is a room four אמות wide and six אמות long.

keyTerms.meaning: A burial place (here, an underground burial cave)
One who takes on a job (a contractor)
A cubit, a measure of length (plural: אַמּוֹת)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who sells a plot of land to another
for him to make himself a burial cave,
and likewise one who takes on a job from another
to make a burial cave for him –
makes the inside of the cave
four cubits by six.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹכֵר מָקוֹם לַחֲבֵרוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ קֶבֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה, separate from the discussion of the mourners' ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no size was set, a burial cave that was sold or ordered is four אמות by six inside.

steps.title: The eight burial niches and their size
steps.stepSummary: Eight niches are dug into the cave walls: three on each long side and two on the far wall. Each is four אמות long and seven טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: He digs eight niches into the cave walls: three on one side, three on the other side, and two on the wall facing the entrance. The niches are four אמות long and seven tall.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It describes the niches dug into the walls of the cave, where the bodies are placed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the size of the main room, the משנה lays out the niches. Three go into each long wall and two into the wall facing the entrance, eight in all. It then starts to give their size: four אמות long and seven high. The sentence continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Burial niches dug into the cave walls
From the wall facing them (opposite the entrance)

phrases.english: And he opens into it eight burial niches –
three from here and three from here,
phrases.notes: These are the two long side walls of the cave.

phrases.english: and two from the wall facing them.
And the niches – their length is four cubits,
and their height is seven,
phrases.notes: The משנה just says 'seven.' It means seven טפחים (handbreadths), not seven אמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 19, moving from the main room to the niches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The cave has eight niches (three, three, and two), each four אמות long and seven טפחים high.
